quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus (Form S-1): revenue was $140.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 versus $10.4 million a year earlier (an increase of 1,252%), and $33.0 million for 2025 versus $19.1 million for 2024 (+73%). 2025 was the first full year of high-performance cloud services for AI workloads; most 2024 revenue came from colocation for institutional crypto-currency miners, a service NScale ceased at the end of 2024. Net losses were $1,020.1 million for the first half of 2026 and $761.8 million for 2025; Adjusted EBITDA was $(199.2) million and $(81.7) million. Cash and cash equivalents were $1.5 billion at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue $140.6 million (H1 2025 $10.4 million, +1,252%); FY2025 revenue $33.0 million (FY2024 $19.1 million, +73%); net loss $1,020.1 million (H1 2026) / $761.8 million (FY2025); Adjusted EBITDA $(199.2) million / $(81.7) million; cash $1.5 billion at June 30, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, revenue by region: for the six months ended June 30, 2026, Portugal $73.0 million, Norway $63.7 million and United Kingdom $3.9 million (52% and 45% of revenue from deployments in Portugal and Norway); for 2025, Norway $31.8 million and United Kingdom $1.2 million (a substantial majority of 2024 and 2025 revenue came from Norway).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026: Portugal $73.0 million, Norway $63.7 million, UK $3.9 million (52% / 45% Portugal / Norway); FY2025: Norway $31.8 million, UK $1.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, customer concentration: the largest customer accounted for 52% of revenue in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 73% of revenue in 2025; in 2024 a single customer accounted for substantially all revenue (93%). The customer that was 73% of 2025 revenue signed a series of GPU infrastructure services agreements from November 2024 through March 2026 (GPU infrastructure and colocation space, phased delivery); NScale anticipates it will be approximately less than 20% of 2026 revenue, with the share expected to keep decreasing. The prospectus does not name the 52% or 73% customer.
quarterly_data.figure: largest customer 52% of H1 2026 revenue; 73% of FY2025 revenue (expected less than 20% of FY2026 revenue); 93% in FY2024

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Pega Nordic: NScale's IPO prospectus says an October 2022 agreement to provide data center infrastructure at its Norway facility was with the customer that represented 93% of 2024 revenue (Pega Nordic named as the counterparty); the agreement terminated in December 2024 and is no longer in effect.
quarterly_data.figure: 93% of FY2024 revenue; agreement terminated December 2024

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, contracted backlog: as of August 31, 2026 it had approximately $2.6 billion of active and $103.4 billion of active and contracted total contract value (TCV) under long-term take-or-pay contracts, versus $0.5 billion and $38.0 billion as of December 31, 2025, supporting approximately 461,000 active or contracted GPUs; weighted average contract life approximately 5.7 years; weighted-average customer prepayment 23% of active and contracted TCV.
quarterly_data.figure: $103.4 billion active and contracted TCV ($2.6 billion active) at August 31, 2026 vs $38.0 billion ($0.5 billion) at December 31, 2025; ~461,000 GPUs; 5.7-year weighted average contract life; 23% weighted-average prepayment

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, remaining performance obligations: RPO for service contracts was $56.4 billion as of June 30, 2026 (including $7.1 billion significant financing component on customer prepayments), expected to be recognized over the next 7 years, versus $34.5 billion at December 31, 2025 (approximately 16% to be recognized in the next two years and 40% in the following two years); plus $2.0 billion of minimum lease payments due from customers under ASC 842 at June 30, 2026. After June 30, 2026 NScale entered into contracts to deploy and operate GPU clusters for an aggregate $52.5 billion (and after December 31, 2025, $62.9 billion).
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $56.4 billion at June 30, 2026 (incl. $7.1 billion financing component; over 7 years); $34.5 billion at December 31, 2025; $2.0 billion minimum lease payments; $52.5 billion of GPU cluster contracts signed after June 30, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, infrastructure footprint as of August 31, 2026: approximately 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs; five active and twelve contracted data center sites (seven wholly-owned, nine colocation, one leased); approximately 1.37 GW of active and contracted capacity (1 GW at owned sites, 200 MW at leased sites, 165 MW at colocation sites), with line of sight to approximately 10 GW of potential power capacity; footprint concentrated in regions such as Norway, Portugal, Iceland, and select locations in the United States and APAC; over 1,000 full-time employees. quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, Monarch Compute Campus: on March 31, 2026 NScale acquired 100% of AIPCorp (American Intelligence & Power Corporation), securing the approximately 2,250-acre Monarch Compute Campus in Mason County, West Virginia - which it believes will be one of the first state-certified AI micro-grids in the United States - with behind-the-meter power; an initial 2 GWs of gross power capacity (1.37 GWs of IT load) is expected online by the first half of 2028, with expansion to approximately 8 GWs of gross capacity planned for 2031 (scalable to over 6.5 GW of IT load power). NScale created Nscale Energy & Power to internalize power origination and development.
quarterly_data.figure: ~2,250 acres; 2 GWs gross / 1.37 GWs IT load by H1 2028; ~8 GWs gross planned for 2031; over 6.5 GW IT load potential

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Caterpillar: NScale's IPO prospectus lists its continued collaboration with Caterpillar as a supplier of natural gas generators among the conditions for realizing the Monarch Compute Campus's behind-the-meter power plan, alongside access to natural gas supply at commercially viable costs.

NScale's IPO prospectus, other acquisitions: on April 24, 2026 it acquired SIN02, a 200 MW powered land site at the SINES Data Campus in Portugal (a 200 MW owned hyperscale campus); in December 2025 it acquired Future Tech, a United Kingdom-based data center engineering consultancy; on July 28, 2026 it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Anyscale (the company behind the Ray open-source distributed AI framework, 740 million cumulative downloads including approximately 174 million in Q2 2026), adding approximately 200 employees, with closing expected at or concurrent with the IPO.
quarterly_data.figure: SIN02 200 MW; Anyscale ~200 employees; Ray 740 million cumulative downloads (~174 million in Q2 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Partner Aker: NScale's IPO prospectus says it formed a 50/50 joint venture with Aker for Stargate Norway, an AI infrastructure project in Kvandal, Norway (agreement July 31, 2025, completed October 8, 2025); in March 2026 the joint venture entities were rolled up into NScale, which acquired Aker's 50% interest. In April 2026 OpenAI withdrew from the Stargate Norway and Stargate UK partnerships.
quarterly_data.figure: 50/50 joint venture; NScale acquired the remaining 50% in March 2026

quarterly_data.signal: NScale's IPO prospectus, commitments as of June 30, 2026: outstanding purchase commitments for technology equipment not yet delivered of $24.0 billion and data center build-out commitments of $3.5 billion, both payable primarily throughout 2026 and 2027, plus $1.4 billion of undiscounted payments for colocation leases not yet commenced.
